summary: This profile from the 'Founder Journeys' series follows Zhang Hua, an artist-turned-entrepreneur who runs the studio Illuminated Canvas in Lanzhou. It traces her path from art student to SME founder, covering her community-building, use of social media and online sales with augmented reality, and her plans for art education and cultural influence.
one_line: Profile of Lanzhou artist Zhang Hua and how she built her studio Illuminated Canvas into a community hub and growing SME.
key_facts: Zhang Hua is an artist and entrepreneur who runs the studio Illuminated Canvas in Lanzhou; the name symbolises how art illuminates lives.
Zhang was born to modest means in October 1987 and her early art attempts met some resistance.
She graduated from Lanzhou City University with a major in Fine Arts in 2008.
After graduating, she traveled through China painting scenes on canvas and sold them at local markets to fund her journey.
On September 15, 2024, Zhang launched Illuminated Canvas, transforming a neglected space in a sunny corner of Lanzhou.
Zhang's goal was an accessible art space where visitors could experience the creation process, not just see finished art.
One of her early pieces, a colorful depiction of the Gobi Desert, reflects how lonely she felt when starting her business.
In her first year she faced financial strain, market skepticism and the challenge of establishing presence in a competitive market.
By December 2025, Illuminated Canvas had become a community hub with workshops, events and art therapy sessions.
The Illuminated Canvas Instagram page debuted in February 2026 and brought international clients and increased sales.
In March 2027, Zhang opened an online shop offering augmented reality views of paintings so customers could see them in their own spaces.
Zhang partnered with local businesses on cross-promotion, public art projects and educational programs.
Zhang plans to make Illuminated Canvas a cultural icon of Lanzhou and advance art education with public schools and local government.
Zhang credits her success to constant learning and now seeks an international customer base through cultural exchange and artistic education.
